# GROMACS - A Molecular Dynamics Package

GROMACS is a versatile package to perform molecular dynamics, i.e., simulate
the Newtonian equations of motion for systems with hundreds to millions of
particles.

## What GROMACS Does

GROMACS is primarily designed for biochemical molecules like proteins, lipids,
and nucleic acids that have a lot of complicated bonded interactions. However,
since GROMACS is extremely fast at calculating the nonbonded interactions
(that usually dominate simulations) many groups are also using it for research
on non-biological systems, e.g., polymers and fluid dynamics.

## Usage

GROMACS includes many tools for preparing, running and analyzing molecular
dynamics simulations. These are all structured as part of a single `gmx`
wrapper binary, invoked with commands like:

    gmx grompp    # Prepare a simulation
    gmx mdrun     # Run a simulation
    gmx help      # Show available commands

If you have installed an MPI version of GROMACS, by default the gmx binary
is called `gmx_mpi` and you should adapt accordingly.

### Basic Workflow

A typical simulation workflow involves:

1. **System Preparation**: Start with a structure file (e.g., PDB format)
2. **Topology Generation**: Generate molecular topology with `gmx pdb2gmx`
3. **Simulation Setup**: Prepare the simulation with `gmx grompp`
4. **Run Simulation**: Execute the dynamics with `gmx mdrun`
5. **Analysis**: Analyze results with various analysis tools

### Key File Types

- `.pdb` - Protein Data Bank structure files
- `.top` - Molecular topology files (complete description of interactions)
- `.gro` - GROMACS coordinate files
- `.xtc`, `.trr` - Trajectory files (simulation output)
- `.mdp` - Molecular dynamics parameter files (simulation settings)
- `.tpr` - Portable binary run input file

### Command-Line Interface

All GROMACS commands require an option before any arguments. Options start
with a single dash (or double dash). For example:

    gmx mdrun -s topol.tpr -v
    gmx grompp -f input.mdp -c conf.gro -p topol.top -o output.tpr

Use `gmx help <command>` or `gmx <command> -h` for detailed help on any tool.

## Features

GROMACS provides:

- **Molecular Dynamics Simulations**: Simulate the time evolution of molecular systems
- **Energy Minimization**: Find stable configurations of molecular systems
- **Free Energy Calculations**: Compute thermodynamic properties
- **Analysis Tools**: Extensive toolkit for trajectory analysis
- **Multiple Force Fields**: Support for various molecular force fields
- **Parallel Computing**: Support for efficient parallel execution

## Resources

- Online documentation: http://manual.gromacs.org/
- Forums: http://forums.gromacs.org/
- Tutorials: http://tutorials.gromacs.org/
- Issue tracking: https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues

## Citation

If you use GROMACS for research, please cite the appropriate papers. See the
CITATION.cff file for complete citation metadata, or visit:
https://www.gromacs.org/articles.html

Key publications include:

- GROMACS: A message-passing parallel molecular dynamics implementation
  H.J.C. Berendsen, D. van der Spoel and R. van Drunen
  Comp. Phys. Comm. 91, 43-56 (1995)
  DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-4655(95)00042-E

- GROMACS 4: Algorithms for highly efficient, load-balanced, and scalable
  molecular simulation
  B. Hess and C. Kutzner and D. van der Spoel and E. Lindahl
  J. Chem. Theory Comput. 4 (2008) pp. 435-447
  DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ct700301q

- GROMACS: High performance molecular simulations through multi-level
  parallelism from laptops to supercomputers
  M. J. Abraham, T. Murtola, R. Schulz, S. Páll, J. C. Smith, B. Hess,
  E. Lindahl, SoftwareX, 1, (2015), 19-25
  DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2015.06.001

## License

GROMACS is free software, distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public
License (LGPL), version 2.1. See the COPYING file for full license text.

SYNOPSIS

gmx grompp [-f [<.mdp>]] [-c [<.gro/.g96/...>]] [-r [<.gro/.g96/...>]]
           [-rb [<.gro/.g96/...>]] [-n [<.ndx>]] [-p [<.top>]]
           [-t [<.trr/.cpt/...>]] [-e [<.edr>]] [-qmi [<.inp>]]
           [-ref [<.trr/.cpt/...>]] [-po [<.mdp>]] [-pp [<.top>]]
           [-o [<.tpr>]] [-imd [<.gro>]] [-[no]v] [-time <real>]
           [-[no]rmvsbds] [-maxwarn <int>] [-[no]zero] [-[no]renum]

DESCRIPTION

gmx grompp (the gromacs preprocessor) reads a molecular topology file, checks
the validity of the file, expands the topology from a molecular description to
an atomic description. The topology file contains information about molecule
types and the number of molecules, the preprocessor copies each molecule as
needed. There is no limitation on the number of molecule types. Bonds and
bond-angles can be converted into constraints, separately for hydrogens and
heavy atoms. Then a coordinate file is read and velocities can be generated
from a Maxwellian distribution if requested. gmx grompp also reads parameters
for gmx mdrun (eg. number of MD steps, time step, cut-off). Eventually a
binary file is produced that can serve as the sole input file for the MD
program.

gmx grompp uses the atom names from the topology file. The atom names in the
coordinate file (option -c) are only read to generate warnings when they do
not match the atom names in the topology. Note that the atom names are
irrelevant for the simulation as only the atom types are used for generating
interaction parameters.

gmx grompp uses a built-in preprocessor to resolve includes, macros, etc. The
preprocessor supports the following keywords:

    #ifdef VARIABLE
    #ifndef VARIABLE
    #else
    #endif
    #define VARIABLE
    #undef VARIABLE
    #include "filename"
    #include <filename>

The functioning of these statements in your topology may be modulated by using
the following two flags in your .mdp file:

    define = -DVARIABLE1 -DVARIABLE2
    include = -I/home/john/doe

For further information a C-programming textbook may help you out. Specifying
the -pp flag will get the pre-processed topology file written out so that you
can verify its contents.

When using position restraints, a file with restraint coordinates must be
supplied with -r (can be the same file as supplied for -c). For free energy
calculations, separate reference coordinates for the B topology can be
supplied with -rb, otherwise they will be equal to those of the A topology.

Starting coordinates can be read from trajectory with -t. The last frame with
coordinates and velocities will be read, unless the -time option is used. Only
if this information is absent will the coordinates in the -c file be used.
Note that these velocities will not be used when gen_vel = yes in your .mdp
file. An energy file can be supplied with -e to read Nose-Hoover and/or
Parrinello-Rahman coupling variables.

gmx grompp can be used to restart simulations (preserving continuity) by
supplying just a checkpoint file with -t. However, for simply changing the
number of run steps to extend a run, using gmx convert-tpr is more convenient
than gmx grompp. You then supply the old checkpoint file directly to gmx mdrun
with -cpi. If you wish to change the ensemble or things like output frequency,
then supplying the checkpoint file to gmx grompp with -t along with a new .mdp
file with -f is the recommended procedure. Actually preserving the ensemble
(if possible) still requires passing the checkpoint file to gmx mdrun -cpi.

binary file is produced that can serve as the sole input file for the MD

SELECTION SYNTAX AND USAGE

Selections are used to select atoms/molecules/residues for analysis. In
contrast to traditional index files, selections can be dynamic, i.e., select
different atoms for different trajectory frames. The GROMACS manual contains a
short introductory section to selections in the Analysis chapter, including
suggestions on how to get familiar with selections if you are new to the
concept. The subtopics listed below provide more details on the technical and
syntactic aspects of selections.

Each analysis tool requires a different number of selections and the
selections are interpreted differently. The general idea is still the same:
each selection evaluates to a set of positions, where a position can be an
atom position or center-of-mass or center-of-geometry of a set of atoms. The
tool then uses these positions for its analysis to allow very flexible
processing. Some analysis tools may have limitations on the types of
selections allowed.

DESCRIPTION

gmx rms compares two structures by computing the root mean square deviation
(RMSD), the size-independent rho similarity parameter (rho) or the scaled rho
(rhosc), see Maiorov & Crippen, Proteins 22, 273 (1995). This is selected by

Each structure from a trajectory (-f) is compared to a reference structure.
The reference structure is taken from the structure file (-s).

With option -mir also a comparison with the mirror image of the reference
structure is calculated. This is useful as a reference for 'significant'
values, see Maiorov & Crippen, Proteins 22, 273 (1995).

Option -prev produces the comparison with a previous frame the specified
number of frames ago.

Option -m produces a matrix in .xpm format of comparison values of each
structure in the trajectory with respect to each other structure. This file
can be visualized with for instance xv and can be converted to postscript with
gmx xpm2ps.

Option -fit controls the least-squares fitting of the structures on top of
each other: complete fit (rotation and translation), translation only, or no
fitting at all.

Option -mw controls whether mass weighting is done or not. If you select the
option (default) and supply a valid .tpr file masses will be taken from there,
otherwise the masses will be deduced from the atommass.dat file in GMXLIB
(deprecated). This is fine for proteins, but not necessarily for other
molecules. You can check whether this happened by turning on the -debug flag
and inspecting the log file.

generates a comparison matrix of one trajectory versus the other.

considered.

actions.command:
cd /tmp/help && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re,os,collections
sections=collections.defaultdict(list)
for f in sorted(os.listdir('.')):
    if not f.endswith('.txt'): continue
    txt=open(f).read()
    # find OPTIONS section
    m=re.search(r'\nOPTIONS\n\n(.*?)(?=\n[A-Z][A-Z ]*\n\n|\Z)', txt, re.S)
    if not m: 
        print("NO OPTIONS:", f); continue
    body=m.group(1)
    cur=None
    for line in body.split('\n'):
        if line.startswith('Options to'):
            cur=line; continue
        if line.startswith(' -'):
            sections[f].append(line)
print(len(sections))
# gather column stats
from collections import Counter
colpos=Counter()
for f,ls in sections.items():
    for l in ls:
        # find start of type part: first char that is '[' or '<' or (if boolean) end
        m=re.match(r'^ -(\S+)(\s*)(.*)$', l)
        name=m.group(1); sp=m.group(2); rest=m.group(3)
        colpos[len(' -'+name+sp)]+=1
print(sorted(colpos.items())[:20])
# show examples of unusual
odd=[]
for f,ls in sections.items():
    for l in ls:
        m=re.match(r'^ -(\S+)(\s*)(.*)$', l)
        if len(' -'+m.group(1)+m.group(2))!=9 and not l.startswith(' -[no]'):
            odd.append((f,l))
print(len(odd))
for x in odd[:20]: print(x)
EOF

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import pty,os,sys
def run(cols, rows=24):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.environ['COLUMNS']=str(cols)
        os.execv('/workspace/./executable', ['/workspace/./executable','-quiet','help','rms'])
    import fcntl,termios,struct
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0,0))
    out=b''
    try:
        while True:
            d=os.read(fd,65536)
            if not d: break
            out+=d
    except OSError: pass
    os.waitpid(pid,0)
    return out.decode()
for cols in (60,80,100,120):
    o=run(cols)
    print("=== cols",cols)
    print('\n'.join(o.split('\n')[3:9]))
EOF

"""Parse the GROMACS command-line help text database into structured option metadata.

The help texts in data/help were captured by observing the reference binary's
command-line output (gmx -quiet help <topic>), which is the permitted way to
learn about the program's interface.
"""
import os, re, sys, json

HELPDIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), 'data', 'help')

def parse_options(text):
    """Return list of option dicts parsed from the OPTIONS section of a help text."""
    m = re.search(r'\nOPTIONS\n\n(.*?)\n\n(?=[A-Z][A-Za-z /-]*\n\n|\Z)', text, re.S)
    if not m:
        return [], []
    body = m.group(1)
    opts = []
    pending = None
    section = None
    notes = []
    for line in body.split('\n'):
        if line.startswith('Options to'):
            section = line
            continue
        if line.startswith(' -'):
            if pending:
                opts.append(pending)
                pending = None
            name = line[2:line.index(' ', 2)] if ' ' in line[2:] else line[2:]
            typ = ''
            idx = 9
            if idx < len(line):
                c = line[idx]
                if c == '[':
                    depth = 1
                    j = idx + 1
                    while j < len(line):
                        if line[j] == '[':
                            depth += 1
                        elif line[j] == ']':
                            depth -= 1
                            if depth == 0:
                                break
                        j += 1
                    typ = line[idx:j + 1]
                elif c == '<':
                    j = line.index('>', idx)
                    typ = line[idx:j + 1]
            default = None
            opt = False
            rest = line[idx + len(typ):]
            d = rest.find('(')
            while d != -1:
                e = rest.find(')', d)
                if e == -1:
                    break
                val = rest[d + 1:e]
                if val == 'Opt.':
                    opt = True
                else:
                    default = val
                rest = rest[e + 1:]
                d = rest.find('(')
            pending = {'name': name.lstrip('[').rstrip(']') if name.startswith('[') else name,
                       'bool': name.startswith('[no]'), 'type': typ, 'default': default,
                       'optional': opt, 'section': section, 'desc': []}
        elif pending is not None and line.startswith(' ' * 11):
            pending['desc'].append(line.strip())
        elif line.strip() == '':
            pass
    if pending:
        opts.append(pending)
    return opts, notes

def desc_extensions(o):
    """Extension list for file options, taken from the description text."""
    txt = ' '.join(o['desc'])
    if not txt or ':' not in txt:
        return []
    tail = txt[txt.rindex(':') + 1:].strip()
    exts = re.split(r'[\s,]+', tail)
    return [e for e in exts if e and re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$', e)]

def desc_enum_values(o):
    txt = ' '.join(o['desc'])
    if not txt or ':' not in txt:
        return []
    tail = txt[txt.rindex(':') + 1:].strip()
    vals = re.split(r'[\s,]+', tail)
    return [v for v in vals if v and re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_.+-]+$', v)]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    for cmd in sys.argv[1:]:
        text = open(os.path.join(HELPDIR, cmd + '.txt')).read()
        opts, notes = parse_options(text)
        print('###', cmd)
        for o in opts:
            print('  %-22s type=%-22s def=%-16s opt=%d ext=%s' % (o['name'], o['type'], o['default'], o['optional'], desc_extensions(o)))

actions.command: cd /workspace/data/help && grep -n 'rot+trans' rms.txt | head; grep -n ' -fit' rms.txt

mkdir -p /workspace/tools && cat > /workspace/tools/survey.py <<'PYEOF'
"""Run the reference binary with a bogus value for each command option and
record how it reacts.  Used to recover option metadata (allowed enum values,
file extensions, required options) purely from observable behaviour."""
import os, re, sys, json, subprocess, time
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from parse_help import parse_options, HELPDIR

BIN = os.environ.get('GMXREF', '/workspace/executable')
OUT = os.environ.get('SURVEY_OUT', '/tmp/survey.json')

def run(args, timeout=10):
    p = subprocess.run([BIN] + args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=timeout)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.decode('utf8', 'replace'), p.stderr.decode('utf8', 'replace')

def error_block(txt):
    m = re.search(r'Error in user input:\n(.*?)\n\nFor more information', txt, re.S)
    if m: return 'input', m.group(1)
    m = re.search(r'((?:System I/O error|Fatal error|File input/output error|Invalid input|Input/Output error|Runtime error|Internal error|API Error)):\n(.*?)\n\nFor more information', txt, re.S)
    if m: return m.group(1), m.group(2)
    return None, None

def parse_opt_errors(body):
    """Split an error block into per-option entries."""
    parts = re.split(r'\n  In (?:command-line )?option ', '\n' + body)
    out = []
    for p in parts[1:]:
        lines = p.split('\n')
        out.append((lines[0].strip(), '\n'.join(lines[1:]).strip()))
    return out

def main():
    cmds = sorted(f[:-4] for f in os.listdir(HELPDIR) if f.endswith('.txt') and not f.startswith('sel_'))
    res = {}
    t0 = time.time()
    for cmd in cmds:
        text = open(os.path.join(HELPDIR, cmd + '.txt')).read()
        opts, notes = parse_options(text)
        entry = {}
        for o in opts:
            if o['bool']:
                continue
            name = o['name']
            rc, so, se = run([cmd, '-' + name, 'ZZZBOGUS'])
            kind, body = error_block(se)
            entry[name] = {'rc': rc, 'kind': kind, 'body': body, 'so': so[:400]}
        res[cmd] = entry
        print('%-20s %d opts %.1fs' % (cmd, len(opts), time.time() - t0), flush=True)
    json.dump(res, open(OUT, 'w'), indent=1)
    print('wrote', OUT, 'elapsed %.1fs' % (time.time() - t0))

main()
PYEOF

        exts=[x.strip() for x in em.group(1).split(',')] if em else []
        lst.append({'opt':name,'stem':stem,'exts':exts})
    out[cmd]=lst

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat > tools/sweep_meta.py <<'PYEOF'
"""Probe option-specific metadata that is not visible in the help text:
  - the set of file extensions GROMACS considers valid at all
  - how many values each <vector> option accepts
"""
import re, os, subprocess, json, sys
BIN = os.environ.get('GMXREF', '/workspace/executable')
def run(args):
    p = subprocess.run([BIN]+args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=15)
    return p.stderr.decode('utf8','replace')

# 1. recognised extensions: test with rms -s (allowed: tpr gro g96 pdb brk ent)
exts = ['tpr','gro','g96','pdb','brk','ent','esp','trr','cpt','tng','xtc','edr','ndx','xvg',
        'xpm','dat','log','top','mdp','itp','inp','tex','eps','m2p','mtx','edi','out','pqr',
        'csv','rtp','h5md','xyz','txt','xyz2','foo','bar2','z','xvg2','dat2','edr2','nd2',
        'pqr2','out2','top2','mdp2','itp2','inp2','tex2','eps2','m2p2','mtx2','edi2','csv2',
        'rtp2','h5md2','g96','gro2','tpr2','pdb2','brk2','ent2','esp2','cpt2','tng2','xtc2',
        'gz','tgz','bz2','xz','Z','json','xml','cfg','idx','npy','npz','h5','bin','rec','sdf',
        'mol','mol2','smi','smiles','xyz.txt','d','f','c','cpp','py','sh','so','o','a','pdf']
res = {}
for e in exts:
    txt = run(['rms','-s','zz.'+e])
    if 'cannot be used for this option' in txt:
        res[e] = 'recognized'
    elif 'does not have a recognizable extension' in txt:
        res[e] = 'unknown'
    elif 'does not exist or is not accessible' in txt:
        res[e] = 'missing'
    else:
        res[e] = 'other:' + txt[:60].replace('\n','|')
json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', 'data', 'exttest.json'),'w'), indent=1)
print('recognized:', sorted([k for k,v in res.items() if v=='recognized']))
print('unknown:', sorted([k for k,v in res.items() if v=='unknown']))
print('missing:', sorted([k for k,v in res.items() if v=='missing']))
print('other:', {k:v for k,v in res.items() if v.startswith('other')})

# 2. vector option value counts
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from parse_help import parse_options, HELPDIR
vec = {}
for f in sorted(os.listdir(HELPDIR)):
    if not f.endswith('.txt') or f.startswith('_topic_') or f.startswith('sel_'): continue
    cmd = f[:-4]
    opts, _ = parse_options(open(os.path.join(HELPDIR,f)).read())
    for o in opts:
        if o['type'] != '<vector>': continue
        counts = {}
        for n in range(1, 7):
            args = [cmd, '-'+o['name']] + ['1']*n
            txt = run(args)
            m = re.search(r'In command-line option -(\S+)\n\s+(.*)', txt)
            if m and m.group(1) == o['name']:
                counts[n] = m.group(2).strip().split('\n')[0]
            else:
                counts[n] = 'OK'

actions.command:
cd /workspace && cat > tools/survey2.py <<'PYEOF'
"""For every command create the files its required options point at and record
what error the reference executable reports next."""
import os, re, json, subprocess, sys, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BIN = os.environ.get('GMXREF', '/workspace/executable')
NOARGS = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'noargs.json')))
work = '/tmp/sv2'
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
os.makedirs(work)
res = {}
for cmd, reqs in sorted(NOARGS.items()):
    for r in reqs:
        ext = r['exts'][0] if r['exts'] else ''
        name = r['stem'] + ('.' + ext if ext else '')
        p = os.path.join(work, name)
        open(p, 'w').close()
    p = subprocess.run([BIN] + [cmd], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=20, cwd=work)
    se = p.stderr.decode('utf8', 'replace')
    m = re.search(r'Program:     (.*)\nSource file: (.*)\nFunction:    (.*)\n\n(.*?):\n(.*?)\n\nFor more', se, re.S)
    so = p.stdout.decode('utf8', 'replace')
    if m:
        res[cmd] = {'prog': m.group(1), 'src': m.group(2), 'func': m.group(3),
                    'kind': m.group(4), 'msg': m.group(5), 'rc': p.returncode, 'so': so[:600]}
    else:
        res[cmd] = {'msg': None, 'rc': p.returncode, 'so': so[:600], 'se': se[:600]}
    print('%-20s %s' % (cmd, (res[cmd]['msg'] or res[cmd]['se'])[:70].replace('\n', '|')), flush=True)
json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'nexterr.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
PYEOF
GMXREF=/workspace/executable timeout 900 python3 tools/survey2.py 2>&1 | tail -40

"""Second stage: create the files required options point at, preferring .gro,

import os, re, json, subprocess, shutil, sys

    3
    1WAT  OW1    1   0.000   0.000   0.000
    1WAT  HW2    2   0.100   0.000   0.000
    1WAT  HW3    3   0.000   0.100   0.000
   1.00000   1.00000   1.00000
"""
work = '/tmp/sv3'
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
os.makedirs(work)
res = {}
for cmd, reqs in sorted(NOARGS.items()):
    for r in reqs:
        exts = [e.lstrip('.') for e in r['exts']]
        ext = 'gro' if 'gro' in exts else (exts[0] if exts else '')
        name = r['stem'] + ('.' + ext if ext else '')
        p = os.path.join(work, name)
        with open(p, 'w') as fh:
            fh.write(GRO if ext == 'gro' else '')
    p = subprocess.run([BIN] + [cmd], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,

"""Second stage: create the files required options point at, preferring .gro,
and record the error that the reference executable reports next."""
import os, re, json, subprocess, shutil, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BIN = os.environ.get('GMXREF', '/workspace/executable')
NOARGS = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'noargs.json')))
GRO = """Test
    3
    1WAT  OW1    1   0.000   0.000   0.000
    1WAT  HW2    2   0.100   0.000   0.000
    1WAT  HW3    3   0.000   0.100   0.000
   1.00000   1.00000   1.00000
"""
work = '/tmp/sv3'
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
os.makedirs(work)
res = {}
for cmd, reqs in sorted(NOARGS.items()):
    for r in reqs:
        exts = [e.lstrip('.') for e in r['exts']]
        ext = 'gro' if 'gro' in exts else (exts[0] if exts else '')
        name = r['stem'] + ('.' + ext if ext else '')
        p = os.path.join(work, name)
        with open(p, 'w') as fh:
            fh.write(GRO if ext == 'gro' else '')
    p = subprocess.run([BIN] + [cmd], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=30, cwd=work)
    se = p.stderr.decode('utf8', 'replace')
    m = re.search(r'Program:     (.*)\nSource file: (.*)\nFunction:    (.*)\n\n(.*?):\n(.*?)\n\nFor more', se, re.S)
    so = p.stdout.decode('utf8', 'replace')
    if m:
        res[cmd] = {'prog': m.group(1), 'src': m.group(2), 'func': m.group(3),
                    'kind': m.group(4), 'msg': m.group(5), 'rc': p.returncode, 'so': so[:800]}
    else:
        res[cmd] = {'msg': None, 'rc': p.returncode, 'so': so[:800], 'se': se[:800]}
    print('%-20s %s' % (cmd, (res[cmd]['msg'] or res[cmd]['se'])[:60].replace('\n', '|')), flush=True)
json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'nexterr_gro.json'), 'w'), indent=1)

PY

for f in os.listdir(HELP):
    if not f.startswith('_topic_'):

    name = f[len('_topic_'):-4]
    args = ['-quiet', 'help'] + (name.split(' ') if name != 'main' else [])

                  'out': open(os.path.join(HELP, f)).read(), 'rc': 0})
# no-arg errors
sv = '/tmp/sv'

    for f in sorted(os.listdir(sv)):
        if not f.endswith('.err'):

        cmd = f[:-4]
        err = open(os.path.join(sv, f)).read()
        rc = 1
        for line in open(os.path.join(sv, 'exits.txt')):

actions.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import json,re,os
OPTS=json.load(open('data/optsurvey.json'))
old=json.load(open('data/noargs.json'))
def ents(body):
    out=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option (\S+)\n', body):
        start=m.end()
        nxt=re.search(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option \S+\n', body[start:])
        end=start+nxt.start() if nxt else len(body)
        seg=body[start:end]
        dm=re.search(r"the default file '([^']*)' does not", seg)
        em=re.search(r"The following extensions were tried to complete the file name:\n\s+(.*)", seg)
        out.append({'opt':m.group(1),'stem':dm.group(1) if dm else None,
                    'exts':[x.strip() for x in em.group(1).split(',')] if em else []})
    return out
new={}
for cmd,entry in OPTS.items():
    seen=[]
    for opt,r in entry.items():
        b=r.get('body') or ''
        if not b.startswith('Invalid input values'): continue
        for e in ents(b):
            if e['opt'] not in [x['opt'] for x in seen]: seen.append(e)
    new[cmd]=seen
json.dump(new, open('data/noargs.json','w'), indent=1)
diff=[c for c in new if [x['opt'] for x in new[c]]!=[x['opt'] for x in old.get(c,[])]]
print("changed:", len(diff))
for c in diff[:20]: print(' ',c, [x['opt'] for x in old.get(c,[])], '->', [x['opt'] for x in new[c]])
print("total reqs:", sum(len(v) for v in new.values()), "commands with reqs:", len([c for c in new if new[c]]))
PY

{"command": "cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import re,os,json
# old: from /tmp/sv captures
old={}
for f in sorted(os.listdir('/tmp/sv')):
    if not f.endswith('.err'): continue
    cmd=f[:-4]
    txt=open('/tmp/sv/'+f).read()
    m=re.search(r'Error in user input:\nInvalid input values\n(.*?)\n\nFor more information', txt, re.S)
    if not m: continue
    body=m.group(1)
    lst=[]
    for p in re.split(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option ', body)[1:]:
        lines=p.split('\n'); name=lines[0].strip(); rest='\n'.join(lines[1:])
        dm=re.search(r"the default file '([^']*)' does not", rest)
        em=re.search(r"The following extensions were tried to complete the file name:\n\s+(.*)", rest)
        lst.append({'opt':name,'stem':dm.group(1) if dm else None,
                    'exts':[x.strip() for x in em.group(1).split(',')] if em else []})
    old[cmd]=lst
# new: from optsurvey
OPTS=json.load(open('data/optsurvey.json'))
def ents(body):
    out=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option (\S+)\n', body):
        start=m.end()
        nxt=re.search(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option \S+\n', body[start:])
        end=start+nxt.start() if nxt else len(body)
        seg=body[start:end]
        dm=re.search(r"the default file '([^']*)' does not", seg)
        em=re.search(r"The following extensions were tried to complete the file name:\n\s+(.*)", seg)
        out.append({'opt':m.group(1),'stem':dm.group(1) if dm else None,
                    'exts':[x.strip() for x in em.group(1).split(',')] if em else []})
    return out
new={}
for cmd,entry in OPTS.items():
    seen=[]
    for opt,r in entry.items():
        b=r.get('body') or ''
        if not b.startswith('Invalid input values'): continue
        for e in ents(b):
            if e['opt'] not in [x['opt'] for x in seen]: seen.append(e)
    new[cmd]=seen
# merge: new first, then old-only
merged={}
for cmd in set(list(old)+list(new)):
    lst=[dict(x) for x in new.get(cmd,[])]
    names=[x['opt'] for x in lst]
    for x in old.get(cmd,[]):
        if x['opt'] not in names: lst.append(x)
    merged[cmd]=lst
json.dump(merged, open('data/noargs.json','w'), indent=1)
print("reqs total", sum(len(v) for v in merged.values()), "cmds", len([c for c in merged if merged[c]]))
print('chi', [x['opt'] for x in merged['chi']], 'grompp', [x['opt'] for x in merged['grompp']], 'saltbr',[x['opt'] for x in merged['saltbr']])
PY"}

actions.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import re,os,json
# old: from /tmp/sv captures
old={}
for f in sorted(os.listdir('/tmp/sv')):
    if not f.endswith('.err'): continue
    cmd=f[:-4]
    txt=open('/tmp/sv/'+f).read()
    m=re.search(r'Error in user input:\nInvalid input values\n(.*?)\n\nFor more information', txt, re.S)
    if not m: continue
    body=m.group(1)
    lst=[]
    for p in re.split(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option ', body)[1:]:
        lines=p.split('\n'); name=lines[0].strip(); rest='\n'.join(lines[1:])
        dm=re.search(r"the default file '([^']*)' does not", rest)
        em=re.search(r"The following extensions were tried to complete the file name:\n\s+(.*)", rest)
        lst.append({'opt':name,'stem':dm.group(1) if dm else None,
                    'exts':[x.strip() for x in em.group(1).split(',')] if em else []})
    old[cmd]=lst
# new: from optsurvey
OPTS=json.load(open('data/optsurvey.json'))
def ents(body):
    out=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option (\S+)\n', body):
        start=m.end()
        nxt=re.search(r'(?:\A|\n)  In option \S+\n', body[start:])
        end=start+nxt.start() if nxt else len(body)
        seg=body[start:end]
        dm=re.search(r"the default file '([^']*)' does not", seg)
        em=re.search(r"The following extensions were tried to complete the file name:\n\s+(.*)", seg)
        out.append({'opt':m.group(1),'stem':dm.group(1) if dm else None,
                    'exts':[x.strip() for x in em.group(1).split(',')] if em else []})
    return out
new={}
for cmd,entry in OPTS.items():
    seen=[]
    for opt,r in entry.items():
        b=r.get('body') or ''
        if not b.startswith('Invalid input values'): continue
        for e in ents(b):
            if e['opt'] not in [x['opt'] for x in seen]: seen.append(e)
    new[cmd]=seen
# merge: new first, then old-only
merged={}
for cmd in set(list(old)+list(new)):
    lst=[dict(x) for x in new.get(cmd,[])]
    names=[x['opt'] for x in lst]
    for x in old.get(cmd,[]):
        if x['opt'] not in names: lst.append(x)
    merged[cmd]=lst
json.dump(merged, open('data/noargs.json','w'), indent=1)
print("reqs total", sum(len(v) for v in merged.values()), "cmds", len([c for c in merged if merged[c]]))
print('chi', [x['opt'] for x in merged['chi']], 'grompp', [x['opt'] for x in merged['grompp']], 'saltbr',[x['opt'] for x in merged['saltbr']])
PY

{"command": "cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
t=open('tools/mk_tests.py').read()
old_start=t.index("sv = '/tmp/sv'")
old_end=t.index("for cmd, entry in OPTS.items():")
new = '''# no-arg behaviour, reconstructed from data/noargs.json
NOARGS = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'noargs.json')))
NA2 = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'noargs2.json'))) \\
      if os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'noargs2.json')) else {}
SV = '/tmp/sv'
for cmd in sorted(set(list(NOARGS) + list(NA2))):
    reqs = NOARGS.get(cmd) or []
    rc = 1
    if SV and os.path.exists(os.path.join(SV, 'exits.txt')):
        for line in open(os.path.join(SV, 'exits.txt')):
            r, c = line.split()
            if c == cmd:
                rc = int(r)
    if reqs:
        text = 'Invalid input values\\n'
        for r in reqs:
            lst = '  ' + ', '.join(r['exts'])
            text += ('  In option %s\\n' % r['opt'])
            text += indentLines('Required option was not provided, and the default file '
                                "'%s' does not exist or is not accessible.\\n"
                                'The following extensions were tried to complete the file '
                                'name:\\n%s' % (r['stem'], lst), '    ') + '\\n'
        cases.append({'name': 'noargs ' + cmd, 'args': ['-quiet', cmd],
                      'err': block('gmx ' + cmd, SRC_FIN, FUNC_FIN, 'Error in user input',
                                   text.rstrip('\\n')), 'rc': rc})
    elif cmd in NA2:
        e = NA2[cmd]
        cases.append({'name': 'noargs ' + cmd, 'args': ['-quiet', cmd],
                      'err': block('gmx ' + cmd, e['src'], e['func'], e['kind'], e['msg']),
                      'rc': rc})
'''
t = t[:old_start] + new + t[old_end:]
open('tools/mk_tests.py','w').write(t)

def wrapText(text, width=78):
    out = []
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        ind = 0
        while ind < len(line) and line[ind] == ' ':
            ind += 1
        words = line.split()
        if not words:
            out.append(' ' * ind)
            continue
        cur = ' ' * ind + words[0]
        for w in words[1:]:
            if len(cur) + 1 + len(w) <= width:
                cur += ' ' + w
            else:
                out.append(cur)
                cur = ' ' * ind + w
        out.append(cur)
    return '\n'.join(out)

cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import re,json
d=json.load(open('data/nexterr_gro.json'))
out={}
for cmd,v in d.items():
    se=v.get('se') or ''
    blocks=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'Program:     (.*?)\nSource file: (.*?)\n(?:Function:    (.*?)\n)?\n(.*?):\n(.*?)\n\nFor more', se, re.S):
        blocks.append({'prog':m.group(1),'src':m.group(2),'func':m.group(3) or '','kind':m.group(4),'msg':m.group(5)})

json.dump(out, open('data/nexterr_full.json','w'), indent=1)
n=sum(1 for v in out.values() if v['blocks'])
print('commands with blocks:', n, 'of', len(out))
import collections
c=collections.Counter((v['blocks'][-1]['src'].split(' (line')[0], v['blocks'][-1]['kind']) for v in out.values() if v['blocks'])
for k,n in c.most_common(8): print(n,k)
PY

"""Test cases for the runtime behaviour of commands whose required files exist."""
import os, re, json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
VER = '2027.0-dev-20260613-384b179-unknown'
RUN = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'runtime.json')))
NOARGS = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'noargs.json')))
GRO = ('Test\n'
       '    3\n'
       '    1WAT    OW1    1   0.000   0.000   0.000\n'
       '    1WAT    HW2    2   0.100   0.000   0.000\n'
       '    1WAT    HW3    3   0.000   0.100   0.000\n'
       '   1.00000   1.00000   1.00000\n')


def block(label, src, func, kind, msg):
    funcline = ('Function:    %s\n' % func) if func else ''
    return ('\n-------------------------------------------------------\n'
            'Program:     %s, version %s\nSource file: %s\n' % (label, VER, src) + funcline + '\n'
            '%s:\n%s\n\nFor more information and tips for troubleshooting, please check the '
            'GROMACS\nwebsite at https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/run-time-errors.html\n'
            '-------------------------------------------------------\n' % (kind, msg))


def wrapText(text, width=78):
    out = []
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        ind = 0
        while ind < len(line) and line[ind] == ' ':
            ind += 1
        words = line.split()
        if not words:
            out.append(' ' * ind)
            continue
        cur = ' ' * ind + words[0]
        for w in words[1:]:
            if len(cur) + 1 + len(w) <= width:
                cur += ' ' + w
            else:
                out.append(cur)
                cur = ' ' * ind + w
        out.append(cur)
    return '\n'.join(out)


cases = []
for cmd, e in sorted(RUN.items()):
    reqs = NOARGS.get(cmd) or []
    d = '/tmp/dt4_' + cmd
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)

        name = r['stem'] + ('.' + ext if ext else '')
        with open(os.path.join(d, name), 'w') as fh:
            fh.write(GRO if ext == 'gro' else '')
    err = block('gmx ' + cmd, e['src'], e['func'], e['kind'], wrapText(e['msg']))
    cases.append({'name': 'run ' + cmd, 'args': ['-quiet', cmd], 'out': e.get('stdout') or '',
                  'err': err, 'rc': e.get('rc', 1), 'cwd': d, 'reset': False})
json.dump(cases, open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'difftest3.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
print(len(cases), 'cases')

def block(label, src, func, kind, msg):
    funcline = ('Function:    %s\n' % func) if func else ''
    return ('\n-------------------------------------------------------\n'
            'Program:     %s, version %s\nSource file: %s\n' % (label, VER, src) + funcline + '\n'
            '%s:\n%s\n\nFor more information and tips for troubleshooting, please check the '
            'GROMACS\nwebsite at https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/run-time-errors.html\n'
            '-------------------------------------------------------\n' % (kind, msg))


def wrapText(text, width=78):
    out = []
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        ind = 0
        while ind < len(line) and line[ind] == ' ':
            ind += 1
        words = line.split()
        if not words:
            out.append(' ' * ind)
            continue
        cur = ' ' * ind + words[0]
        for w in words[1:]:
            if len(cur) + 1 + len(w) <= width:
                cur += ' ' + w
            else:
                out.append(cur)
                cur = ' ' * ind + w
        out.append(cur)
    return '\n'.join(out)

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat > docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md <<'EOF'
# Implementation notes

This tree contains a from-scratch reimplementation of the `gmx` command line
driver of the reference build.  Everything that is reproduced here was learned
by running the reference executable through its documented command line
interface and recording what it printed:

* `gmx -quiet help <topic>` for every command and help topic
  (captured in `data/help/*.txt`),
* invoking every command without arguments, with a bogus value for every option
  and with the files its required options point at
  (`tools/survey*.py`, results in `data/*.json`),
* the startup banner, the extended version information and the copyright text
  (`data/version.txt`, `data/cop_full.txt`).

## Layout

    compile.sh          builds ./executable (needs only python3 and g++)
    src/gmx.h           interfaces shared by the driver
    src/main.cpp        argument handling, module dispatch, exit codes
    src/options.cpp     command line parser and option validation
    src/util.cpp        formatting, word wrap, error blocks, startup header
    src/commands.cpp    per command behaviour and error emulation
    src/version.cpp     version and copyright text (generated)
    src/quotes.cpp      quote list used for the "GROMACS reminds you" footer
    src/gmxdata.cpp     help texts, option tables and error tables (generated)
    tools/gen_*.py      generate the tables above from data/
    tools/difftest.py   regression tests against the recorded expectations

## Command line parsing

The parser follows the behaviour that was observed:

* an argument is an option name when it starts with `-`, is longer than one
  character, is not made only of dashes and does not parse as a number;
* boolean options never take a value from a plain word, but a following
  negative number is reported as an invalid value;
* value options consume all following arguments that are not option names,
  reporting `Invalid value` for the ones that do not convert and
  `Too many values` for the ones beyond the allowed count;
* errors are collected and reported together, except that a positional
  argument and a value that cannot be converted abort the parse;
* input files are checked for existence (with extension completion) only for
  the options that the tool requires to exist, which was determined per option
  from the recorded behaviour.

## Data files

`data/` holds the observations that the code is built from.  They are plain
text/JSON, generated by the scripts in `tools/` while the behaviour of the
reference program was being explored.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Document the implementation" && echo committed"}
